statement:
Let $\delta^{\mathbf{no\ iso}}_k(n)$ denote the minimum-degree threshold such that the $k$-switch graph of an $n$-vertex graph, when nonempty, is guaranteed to have positive minimum degree. **Isolated-matching threshold conjecture.** There exists $c>0$ such that, for all $k$ and $n$,

$$
\delta^{\mathbf{no\ iso}}_k(n)\in[n/k-c,n/k+c].
$$

The conjecture is motivated by the semidegree version of the Caccetta–Häggkvist conjecture, which is equivalent to the corresponding no-isolated-vertices threshold for balanced bipartite graphs. The general-graph threshold remains open.
title: General-graph isolated-matching threshold conjecture
source_name: Ross J. Kang and Clément Legrand-Duchesne, “Dirac's theorem and the switch geometry of perfect matchings”, arXiv:2604.17911 (2026).
reason: Uniform additive constant for all k,n requires switch-graph control related to semidegree cycle thresholds. No finite isolated matching would establish the uniform claim without definitions and a scalable obstruction; no such mechanism found.

statement: Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$ with $n\geq 3$, and let $\mathcal{G}=\{G_i:i\in[n]\}$ be a family of $n$-vertex graphs with the same vertex set; the graphs in the family may be identical. For a graph $G$, let $\sigma(G)$ denote the minimum, over all nonadjacent vertex pairs $u,v$, of $d_G(u)+d_G(v)$. **Rainbow Hamiltonian cycle conjecture.** If $\sigma(G_i)\geq n$ for every $i\in[n]$, then $\mathcal{G}$ contains a rainbow Hamiltonian cycle. This extends Ore's Hamiltonicity condition from a single graph to a family of graphs; the supplied text gives no resolution, so the conjecture is recorded as open.
title: Rainbow Hamiltonian cycle conjecture for graph families satisfying an Ore-type condition
source_name: Luyi Li, Yubo Wang and Guiying Yan, “Pancyclicity in Graph Families with the Ore-Type Condition”, arXiv:2604.27535 (2026).
reason: Each of n graphs meets Ore's degree-sum condition, but separate Hamilton cycles do not supply distinct edge colors. A color-exchange absorption argument for arbitrary families remains missing; identical-graph cases give no full result.

statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, and let $\ell\geq 2$ be fixed. Consider graphs on $2n+1$ vertices, and say that two vertices are joined by a path of length $2\ell+1$ when such a path has those vertices as its endpoints. **Chen and Ma's conjecture.** For sufficiently large $n$, the maximum number of edges in a graph that does not contain two vertices of the same degree joined by a path of length $2\ell+1$ is at most $n^2+n$.

The case of paths of length three was proved by Chen and Ma for $n\geq 600$, with the bound later improved to $n\geq 2$ by Liu and Zeng. The conjecture extends this extremal equal-degree-endpoint problem to every fixed odd path length; the source paper states that it confirms the conjecture.
title: Chen and Ma's conjecture on equal-degree endpoints joined by odd paths
source_name: Xiamiao Zhao, Yichen Wang and Mei Lu, “A generalization of Erdős-Hajnal problem on paths with equal-degree endpoints”, arXiv:2605.03825 (2026).
reason: Primary Conjecture1.2 and Theorem1.3 match all fixed ell>=3 for sufficiently large n; ell=2 is explicitly credited to Liu–Zeng. No new outcome. Selected theorem passage read, not the complete proof or cited ell=2 body.

statement:
Let $r_4(5,n)$ be the smallest integer $N$ such that every $N$-vertex $4$-uniform hypergraph contains either a copy of $K_5^{(4)}$ or an independent set of size $n$. **Mubayi–Suk conjecture.** For every $n\ge5$, there is an absolute constant $c>0$ such that

$$
r_4(5,n)\ge 2^{2^{n^c}}.
$$

This conjecture seeks a double-exponential lower bound for the remaining difficult case $r_4(5,n)$ and would close the relevant exponential gap up to the precise exponent in the innermost term. The source does not state a resolution.
title: Mubayi–Suk double-exponential lower-bound conjecture for $r_4(5,n)$
source_name: Chunchao Fan, Mingze Li, Qizhong Lin and Bo Ning, “An improved double-exponential lower bound for r_4(5,n)”, arXiv:2605.04105 (2026).
reason: Double-exponential growth requires a scalable 4-uniform construction for every n>=5 with an absolute exponent; finite Ramsey instances cannot certify it. The source title suggests progress but was not treated as proof-body evidence.

statement:
Let $\mu(g)$ be the maximum order of a purely non-free (gpnf) action on a closed orientable surface of genus $g$. For even $g\geq 2$, the paper proves that either $\mu(g)=8g$ or

$$
\mu(g)=\frac{8n}{n-4}(g-1)
$$

for some integer $n>4$, and that the latter case occurs for only finitely many $g$ for each fixed $n$.

**Eventual 8g conjecture.**

$$
\mu(g)=8g
$$

for all but finitely many $g$. The authors additionally suggest that this may hold for all $g$. The preceding results leave open whether infinitely many values of $n$ can produce the exceptional form; this conjecture asserts that such exceptions occur only finitely often overall.
title: The eventual 8g conjecture for purely non-free actions
source_name: C. Bagiński, G. Gromadzki and R. A. Hidalgo, “On the biggest purely non-free conformal actions on compact Riemann surfaces and their asymptotic properties”, arXiv:2605.04214 (2026).
reason: Even-genus qualification and purely-non-free action definitions require primary comparison. Finiteness for each fixed signature n does not imply finiteness over all signatures; no uniform signature bound found. Odd-genus wording changes earn no credit.

statement:
Let $\triangle$ be a triangle, with area $|\triangle|$, perimeter $|\partial\triangle|$, and first Dirichlet eigenvalue $\lambda_1(\triangle)$. Define

$$
\mathcal{F}(\triangle):=\lambda_1(\triangle)|\triangle|-\frac{\pi^2}{16}\frac{|\partial\triangle|^2}{|\triangle|}.
$$

**Laugesen–Siudeja's conjecture.** The functional $\mathcal{F}(\triangle)$ is minimized uniquely by the equilateral triangle, and its minimum value is $7\sqrt{3}\pi^2/12$. This is a sharp quantitative refinement of Makai's inequality for triangles; the source gives no evidence that the conjecture has been resolved.
title: Laugesen–Siudeja's sharp area-perimeter eigenvalue conjecture for triangles
source_name: Ryoki Endo, Xuefeng Liu and Phanuel Mariano, “Sharp Dirichlet eigenvalue inequalities on triangles”, arXiv:2605.04331 (2026).
reason: Universal sharp spectral inequality on all triangles needs analytic control over degenerating shapes and uniqueness. An equilateral evaluation only checks normalization and cannot settle shape minimization.

statement:
Let $q$ be a prime power. In the strong $(m,n)_q$-Tic-Tac-Toe game on the affine space $4\mathbb{F}_q^m4$, let $T(n,q)$ denote the smallest dimension $m$ for which the first player has a winning strategy. **Exponential threshold conjecture.** For every prime power $q$, there exists a constant $C_q>0$ such that

$$
T(n,q)\le C_q q^n
$$

for every $n\ge 1$. The conjecture is motivated by the known exponential upper bound for $q=2$ and the corresponding Erdős–Selfridge lower bound; establishing such an upper bound for every prime power remains open.
title: Exponential upper-bound conjecture for the strong Tic-Tac-Toe threshold
source_name: Luca Bastioni, Alessandro Giannoni and Javier Lobillo-Olmedo, “Thresholds for Tic-Tac-Toe on Finite Affine Spaces”, arXiv:2605.05455 (2026).
reason: Need a first-player strategy with dimension C_q q^n simultaneously for every n at each prime power. A strategy for q=2 or a finite board is insufficient; no uniform strategy found.

statement: For a graph $H$, let $\chi(H)$ denote its chromatic number and $|H|$ its number of vertices. A graph $G$ is **$H$-good** if $R(G,H)=\max\{(|G|-1)(\chi(H)-1)+\sigma(H),(|H|-1)(\chi(G)-1)+\sigma(G)\}$, where $\sigma(F)$ is the minimum size of a color class in a proper $\chi(F)$-coloring of $F$. **Allen–Brightwell–Skokan's conjecture.** For any graph $H$ and $m\geq \chi(H)|H|$, the cycle $C_m$ is $H$-good. The conjecture would extend the known theory of Ramsey goodness to cycles against arbitrary graphs; the source presents it as open, including the cases relevant to $H=K_{2,n}$.
title: Allen–Brightwell–Skokan cycle goodness conjecture
source_name: Abisek Dewan, Sayan Gupta and Rajiv Mishra, “On Ramsey goodness of K_2,n versus cycles”, arXiv:2605.06253 (2026).
reason: Arbitrary H and all m>=chi(H)|H| require general Ramsey goodness. Bipartite or complete target cases do not resolve it; no full extremal mechanism found.

statement:
Let an **Eulerian digraph** be a directed graph in which every vertex has equal in-degree and out-degree, and let the **strong immersion** relation be the relation described in the paper. For $d\geq 1$, consider the class of Eulerian digraphs of maximum degree $2d$.

**Johnson's conjecture.** For every $d\geq 1$, the class of Eulerian digraphs of maximum degree $2d$ is well-quasi-ordered by strong immersion.

This conjecture would establish well-quasi-ordering for every bounded-degree class of Eulerian digraphs under strong immersion, complementing the paper's antichain showing that unbounded degree prevents such a result. It was previously conjectured by Johnson; the source gives no resolution.
title: Johnson's bounded-degree Eulerian digraph immersion conjecture
source_name: Dario Cavallaro, Ken-ichi Kawarabayashi and Stephan Kreutzer, “Well-Quasi-Ordering Eulerian Digraphs: Bounded Carving Width”, arXiv:2605.07468 (2026).
reason: For each bounded degree, must rule out every infinite strong-immersion antichain of Eulerian digraphs. Finite tests cannot certify well-quasi-ordering and no structural reduction available.

statement: For each $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $X_n\subset\mathbb{R}_n^+$ be the largest subsemigroup containing $\mathcal{H}_n$ and $\mathbb{I}_n$ such that, for every $m\leq n$, Hadamard multiplication by an element of $X_n$ maps $\mathcal{H}_m$ into $\mathcal{H}_m$. Let $Y_n$ be the family of polynomials defined in the paper, with $Y_1=X_1$, $Y_2=X_2$, $Y_3=X_3$, and $Y_4=X_4$. **The idealizer conjecture.** For any $n\in\mathbb{N}$, equality $Y_n=X_n$ holds. The cases $n\leq 4$ are established in the paper, while the conjecture proposes the equality for all degrees.
title: The idealizer conjecture for stable polynomials
source_name: Michał Kudra, “The idealizer of the semigroup of stable polynomials”, arXiv:2605.07628 (2026).
reason: X_n is universal over Hadamard actions on all H_m and Y_n is only source-defined. Need literal Y_n inequalities before searching degree5 counterexamples; low-degree equalities are given and uncredited.

statement:
Let $D_{\mathrm{mono}}(n)$ denote the exact maximum number of points in a monochromatic no-three-in-line configuration on the checkerboard grid of side length $n$, and let $\alpha$ be the middle real root of

$$
401\alpha^3-1744\alpha^2+2240\alpha-768=0.
$$

**Monochromatic NTIL asymptotics.** The exact monochromatic no-three-in-line maxima satisfy

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{D_{\mathrm{mono}}(n)}{n}=\alpha.
$$

This is stronger than the corresponding relaxation asymptotics: the finite LP computations motivate it, while the continuum certificate gives an exact upper bound only for the odd-fat relaxation. The discrete limit remains unproved.
title: Monochromatic no-three-in-line asymptotics
source_name: Thomas Prellberg, “No-three-in-line sets on the checkerboard grid”, arXiv:2605.09215 (2026).
reason: Exact discrete asymptotic needs both construction and upper bound at a cubic irrational constant. Odd-fat relaxation certificate alone cannot prove integrality or asymptotic attainability.

statement: Let a **hole** be a chordless cycle of length at least four; it is even if its length is even. For an integer $k\geqslant 2$, a graph $G$ with at least one edge is **$k$-divisible** if, for every induced subgraph $H$ with at least one edge, $V(H)$ can be partitioned into $k$ sets, none of which contains a maximum clique of $H$. **Hoàng's conjecture.** Every even-hole-free graph is $3$-divisible. This conjecture concerns structural decompositions of even-hole-free graphs and the resulting chromatic bounds; the supplied text gives no resolution, so its status remains open.
title: Hoàng's 3-divisibility conjecture for even-hole-free graphs
source_name: Hongzhang Chen, Kaiyang Lan and Wenlong Zhong, “On two conjectures of Hoàng”, arXiv:2605.09293 (2026).
reason: Every induced subgraph must admit a three-part maximum-clique-avoiding partition. A coloring of the input alone is not this hereditary property; no uniform even-hole-free decomposition found.

statement: Let $G$ be a graph, let $k$ be a positive integer, and let $L$ be a $k$-list assignment for $G$. Write $m:=\left\lceil\frac{|G|}{k}\right\rceil$. An $L$-coloring is **$m$-bounded** if every color is used on at most $m$ vertices; $G$ is equitably list $k$-colorable (EL $k$-colorable) if it has an $m$-bounded $L$-coloring for every $k$-list assignment $L$. Here $\Delta(G)$ denotes the maximum degree of $G$. **Kostochka–Pelsmajer–West conjecture.** Every graph $G$ is EL $k$-colorable for each $k>\Delta(G)$. This is the list analogue of equitable colorability and was proposed by Kostochka, Pelsmajer and West. Its resolution is not specified in the supplied text.
title: Kostochka–Pelsmajer–West conjecture on equitable list colorability
source_name: H. A. Kierstead, Alexandr Kostochka and Zimu Xiang, “An introduction to equitable DP coloring of graphs”, arXiv:2605.17783 (2026).
reason: Arbitrary k-lists with k>Delta and global color quotas require simultaneous equitable allocation. Ordinary Hajnal–Szemeredi or ordinary list colorability does not bridge these constraints.

statement: Let $varphi(x,y)$ be a partitioned formula, and let $f_{varphi}(k,l)$ denote the number of pairwise-inconsistent partial $varphi$-types of size $k$ over a parameter set of size $l$. For $tin\boldsymbol{N}$, let $\bigwedge_tvarphi$ denote the associated $t$-fold conjunction formula. **Counting-types conjecture.** The following are equivalent: (i) $\bigwedge_tvarphi$ is NTP$_2$ for every $tin\boldsymbol{N}$; (ii) $f_{\bigwedge_tvarphi}(k,l)$ is polynomially bounded for every $tin\boldsymbol{N}$. At minimum, $f_{varphi}(k,l)$ should be polynomially bounded for every formula in an NTP$_2$ theory. The paper proves that polynomial boundedness follows from ULCFS and obtains an $varepsilon$-power-saving result, but the proposed characterization is open.
title: Counting-types characterization of NTP$_2$
source_name: Artem Chernikov and Chuyin Jiang, “Fractional Helly property and combinatorics of forking in NTP_2 theories”, arXiv:2605.18123 (2026).
reason: Literal statement loses TeX commands and does not specify the variables of the polynomial bound. The metadata's refuted label conflicts with prose and supplies no witness. Exact NTP2/conjunction definitions and primary counterexample body needed.

statement:
For a fixed base $b\geq 2$, define the **Nnamlerinchs constant** $\overleftarrow{K}_b$ to be the smallest number greater than $1$ such that every sufficiently large integer can be written as the sum of at most $\overleftarrow{K}_b$ reversed primes in base $b$. **Nnamlerinchs constant existence conjecture.** For every $b\geq 2$,

$$
\overleftarrow{K}_b<\infty.
$$

The paper notes that this is much weaker than the pure reversed-prime representation conjecture, but it is not known whether the constant is finite for any general base. A theorem in the paper shows that along an infinite sequence of bases the constants, when defined, have lower bounds of order $\log b$.
title: Existence of the Nnamlerinchs constant
source_name: Michael Harm and Daniel R. Johnston, “The reverse Goldbach problem and a refined Zsiflaw–Legeis theorem”, arXiv:2605.21876 (2026).
reason: Must obtain a finite additive basis of reversed primes in every base. Ordinary prime additive-basis theorems do not preserve reversed digits; no density/transference route justified.

statement:
For a fixed base $b\geq 2$, let $\overleftarrow{K}_b$ be the smallest number greater than $1$ such that every sufficiently large integer is a sum of at most $\overleftarrow{K}_b$ reversed primes in base $b$. **Nnamlerinchs constant upper-bound conjecture.** For every $b\geq 2$,

$$
\overleftarrow{K}_b\ll\log b.
$$

This conjecture strengthens the existence conjecture by proposing a uniform logarithmic upper bound. The paper proves that on an infinite increasing sequence of bases, the constants have a matching lower bound $\overleftarrow{K}_{b_i}\gg\log b_i$, so the predicted order would be sharp along that sequence.
title: Logarithmic upper bound for the Nnamlerinchs constant
source_name: Michael Harm and Daniel R. Johnston, “The reverse Goldbach problem and a refined Zsiflaw–Legeis theorem”, arXiv:2605.21876 (2026).
reason: Uniform O(log b) bound is stronger than existence for each base; known lower bounds along a sequence do not give an upper bound. No constructive reversed-prime decomposition found.

statement: For $k\ge 1$ and any tree $T$ of order $m$, let $G$ be a $k$-connected graph with minimum degree $delta(G)\ge \left\lfloor 3k/2\right\rfloor+m-1$. A subtree $T'$ is **isomorphic** to $T$ when $T'\cong T$. **Mader's tree-removability conjecture.** Every such graph $G$ contains a subtree $T'\cong T$ such that $G-V(T')$ is $k$-connected. This extends Mader's path-removability theorem from paths to arbitrary trees. The conjecture is known for paths, for $k=1$, for particular families of trees, for $2$-connected graphs, and for $k\le 3$; it remains open for $k\ge 4$.
title: Mader's tree-removability conjecture
source_name: Hengzhe Li, Mingming Zhou, Shinya Fujita and Yaping Mao, “From Halin's Edge Removability to Matching Removability in k-Connected Graphs”, arXiv:2605.24035 (2026).
reason: Arbitrary tree and every connectivity k with exact degree threshold require preserving all k-separators after deletion. Paths or k<=3 are already credited source cases, not full-scope progress.

statement:
For a fixed integer $r\ge 2$, let $K_r$ denote the complete graph on $r$ vertices, and let $\alpha^*(K_r)$ be the minimum-degree threshold of Hamiltonicity for perturbation by a uniformly random $K_r$-factor. **Espuny Díaz and Girão's conjecture.** For all $r\ge 2$, $\alpha^*(K_r)$ is the unique real positive solution to

$$
x^r+rx-1=0.
$$

This conjecture generalizes the known case $\alpha^*(K_2)=\sqrt{2}-1$, and predicts the Hamiltonicity threshold for random clique-factor perturbations for every fixed clique size. Its status is not resolved in the supplied source.
title: Espuny Díaz and Girão's Hamiltonicity threshold conjecture for random clique-factors
source_name: Dingjia Mao, Feihong Yuan and Wenling Zhou, “Pancyclicity of graphs perturbed by a random F-factor”, arXiv:2606.02160 (2026).
reason: Polynomial's unique positive root is elementary but identifying the random K_r-factor Hamiltonicity threshold for every r is the substantive gap. A root computation would only be a helper.

statement:
Let $X$ be the set on which the permutations act, let $\operatorname{Sym}(X)$ be its symmetric group, let $F(g)$ be the free energy associated with $g\in\operatorname{Sym}(X)$, and let $\pi$ be the reflection permutation. The parameters $q$ and $n$ specify the tensor-network model.

**Reflection-permutation conjecture.** The reflection permutation $\pi$ gives the true minimum for all $(q,n)$, namely

$$
\min_{g\in\operatorname{Sym}(X)} F(g)=F(\pi).
$$

The conjecture identifies the minimizer of the free energy with the reflection permutation. In the supplied discussion this is motivated by the analysis of the $n=2$ case and the lower bound associated with the multiway-cut conjecture, but no resolution is stated.
title: The reflection-permutation conjecture for the free energy of random tensor networks
source_name: Miao Hu, Simon Lin and Ion Nechita, “Multi-entropy in random tensor networks”, arXiv:2606.04470 (2026).
reason: F, permutation domain X, allowed q,n and reflection are not defined literally beyond source references. Cannot run a meaningful permutation minimization or claim counterexample before recovering the model.

statement:
For each fixed integer $k\ge 6$, let $h_k(n)$ be the maximum number of $k$-holes determined by a planar point set in general position of size at most $n$ and containing no $(k+1)$-hole. A $k$-hole is a $k$-element subset in convex position whose convex hull contains no other point of the set.

**Exponent conjecture for $h_k(n)$.** For every fixed integer $k\ge 6$,

$$
h_k(n)=O_k\!\left(n^{\lceil k/3 \rceil}\right).
$$

The paper proves upper and lower bounds with exponents $\lceil k/2\rceil$ and $\lfloor k/3\rfloor$, respectively, and conjectures that the true exponent is closer to the lower bound. Horton sets and grid Horton sets provide supporting examples, but the asserted upper bound remains open.
title: Exponent conjecture for k-holes avoiding a (k+1)-hole
source_name: Andrew Suk and Su Zhou, “On the maximum number of k-holes in point sets with no (k + 1)-hole”, arXiv:2606.05721 (2026).
reason: For each fixed k>=6 need improve the exponent from ceil(k/2) to ceil(k/3) uniformly over all point sets with no (k+1)-hole. Checking Horton configurations would only examine a construction subclass.

statement:
For $cdelta cin (0,1)$ and $Ncinmathbb{N}$, let $cphi_{cdelta}(N)$ be the largest integer such that every set $Acsubseteq [N]$ with $|A|cgeq cdelta N$ contains a sumset $B+C$, where $B,Ccsubseteq [N]$ and $cminc{|B|,|C|cgeq cphi_{cdelta}(N)$. **Kra–Moreira–Richter–Robertson conjecture.** For every $cdeltacin(0,1)$,

$$
0<climinf_{Nctocinfty}\frac{cphi_{cdelta}(N)}{clog(N)}
$$

and

$$
climsup_{Nctocinfty}\frac{cphi_{cdelta}(N)}{clog(N)}<cinfty.
$$

This conjecture asserts that the largest guaranteed summands in dense finite subsets of $[N]$ have logarithmic order, bounded above and below by positive constants depending on the density. It was posed by Kra, Moreira, Richter and Robertson; its resolution is not established in the supplied source.
title: Kra–Moreira–Richter–Robertson logarithmic growth conjecture for finite sumsets
source_name: Felipe Hernández and Luke Hetzel, “On growth rates of infinite and finite sumsets”, arXiv:2606.07310 (2026).
reason: Need positive logarithmic lower and finite logarithmic upper constants for each fixed density. Corrupted literal TeX does not supply a finite exact extremal route; finite sumset searches cannot prove both limiting bounds.

statement:
Let $s,a,b,t$ be integers satisfying $s<a\leq b$. For graphs $K_{a,b}$ and $K_{s,t}$, write $\mathrm{ex}(n,K_{a,b},K_{s,t})$ for the maximum number of copies of $K_{a,b}$ in an $n$-vertex $K_{s,t}$-free graph.

**Generalized Turán number exponent conjecture.** There exists $t_0$ such that, for all $t\geq t_0$,

$$
\mathrm{ex}(n,K_{a,b},K_{s,t})=\Theta_{s,t,a,b}(n^s).
$$

The preceding theorem proves this assertion for $s\in\{2,3\}$ when $t$ is sufficiently large. The conjecture extends that result to all $s<a\leq b$, and the source gives no resolution in the general case.
title: Generalized Turán number exponent conjecture
source_name: Oliver Janzer, Sean Longbrake and Liana Yepremyan, “On the generalized Turán number of complete bipartite graphs”, arXiv:2606.09801 (2026).
reason: All s<a<=b and sufficiently large t require matching n^s generalized Turan bounds. s=2,3 are source-known; no uniform higher-s construction/counting argument found.

statement:
Let $G$ be a **$K_3$-divisible graph**, meaning that $3$ divides $e(G)$ and $2$ divides $d_G(v)$ for every vertex $v$, with $n$ vertices and minimum degree $delta(G)$. A **$K_3$-decomposition** is a partition of the edges of $G$ into edge-disjoint triangles.

**Nash-Williams' conjecture.** If $G$ is $K_3$-divisible and

$$
\delta(G) \geq \frac{3}{4}n,
$$

then, for sufficiently large $n$, $G$ admits a $K_3$-decomposition.

This is the central extremal conjecture in design theory. The paper presents a proof of the associated fractional conjecture, while the integral statement remains the target motivating the work.
title: Nash-Williams' conjecture for triangle decompositions
source_name: Michelle Delcourt and Luke Postle, “A Proof of Nash-Williams' Conjecture”, arXiv:2606.11178 (2026).
reason: Primary Theorem1.8 explicitly asserts full Nash–Williams conjecture; Section12.2 assembly proof read against delta>=3n/4 and K3-divisibility. Theorems12.4–12.8 and their substantial dependencies were not audited. Public full-scope theorem defeats a discovery proposal here.

statement:
Let $G$ be a **$K_3$-divisible graph**, meaning that $3$ divides $e(G)$ and every vertex has even degree. The **girth** of a $K_3$-decomposition is the smallest integer $g$ for which some $g$ triangles span at most $g+2$ vertices.

**Erdős meets Nash-Williams' conjecture.** For every integer $g$, every sufficiently large $K_3$-divisible graph $G$ on $n$ vertices satisfying

$$
\delta(G)\geq \frac{3n}{4}
$$

admits a $K_3$-decomposition with girth at least $g$.

This conjecture combines the high-girth Steiner triple system problem with Nash-Williams' minimum-degree problem. The source presents it as a conjectural common generalization; no resolution is supplied for the exact $3n/4$ threshold.
title: Erdős meets Nash-Williams' conjecture for high-girth triangle decompositions
source_name: Michelle Delcourt and Luke Postle, “A Proof of Nash-Williams' Conjecture”, arXiv:2606.11178 (2026).
reason: High-girth decompositions at exact 3n/4 remain stronger than source's stated asymptotic corollary with epsilon slack. Literal girth wording includes trivial configurations unless conventional exclusions supplied; no credit for this wording issue.

statement:
Let $G$ be a **$d$-regular graph** on $n$ vertices, with even degree $d$, and let $F$ be a **2-regular graph** on $n$ vertices, meaning every vertex of $F$ has degree two. A decomposition of $G$ into copies of $F$ is a partition of $E(G)$ into edge-disjoint subgraphs each isomorphic to $F$.

**Approximate Oberwolfach Nash-Williams' conjecture.** For every $\varepsilon>0$, for all sufficiently large $n$, if

$$
d\geq\left(\frac{3}{4}+\varepsilon\right)n,
$$

then every such $d$-regular graph $G$ decomposes into edge-disjoint copies of $F$.

This is the minimum-degree analogue of the Oberwolfach problem and generalizes Nash-Williams' conjecture. The source cites substantial partial progress but does not state a resolution of this approximate conjecture.
title: Approximate Oberwolfach Nash-Williams' conjecture
source_name: Michelle Delcourt and Luke Postle, “A Proof of Nash-Williams' Conjecture”, arXiv:2606.11178 (2026).
reason: Full edge decomposition into any n-vertex 2-factor at (3/4+epsilon)n is stronger than packing (1-o(1))e(G) edges. Source application discussion does not close the leftover absorption gap; no proof claimed.

statement:
Let $G=(V,E,\pi)$ be a Borel multigraph of maximum degree $\Delta\in{\mathbb N}$ with an **unbalanced bipartition** $(A,B)$, meaning that the two sides have unequal relative sizes in the sense used for the paper's measurable matching theorem. For a probability measure $\mu$ on $V$, let $\chi'_\mu(G)$ denote the measurable edge-chromatic number.

**Unbalanced bipartite measurable edge-coloring conjecture.** For every probability measure $\mu$ on $V$,

$$
\chi'_\mu(G)\leqslant\Delta.
$$

This conjecture extends the paper's measurable matching theorem. König's theorem gives the same bound combinatorially for bipartite multigraphs, so the issue is whether the edge-coloring can be chosen measurably.
title: The unbalanced bipartite measurable edge-coloring conjecture
source_name: Anton Bernshteyn, Matt Bowen and Felix Weilacher, “Measurable matchings in unbalanced graphs”, arXiv:2606.11558 (2026).
reason: Unbalanced means the source's measurable expansion condition, not merely unequal finite sides. Konig's finite theorem does not provide a measurable Delta-edge-coloring for every probability measure; primary definitions needed.

statement:
Let $G=(V,E,\pi)$ be a simple Borel graph of maximum degree $\Delta\in{\mathbb N}$. Assume that no two vertices of degree $\Delta$ in $G$ are adjacent. For a probability measure $\mu$ on $V$, let $\chi'_\mu(G)$ denote the measurable edge-chromatic number.

**Nonadjacent maximum-degree measurable edge-coloring conjecture.** For every probability measure $\mu$ on $V$,

$$
\chi'_\mu(G)\leqslant\Delta.
$$

The paper presents this as a stronger conjectural measurable analogue of the classical edge-coloring bound for simple graphs. Its status is open.
title: The nonadjacent maximum-degree measurable edge-coloring conjecture
source_name: Anton Bernshteyn, Matt Bowen and Felix Weilacher, “Measurable matchings in unbalanced graphs”, arXiv:2606.11558 (2026).
reason: Nonadjacent maximum-degree vertices give a finite edge-coloring intuition but arbitrary Borel graph and every measure require measurable choices. No measurable matching iteration with preserved hypotheses justified.

statement:
Let $D(k,\mathbb{Z}^2)$ denote the maximum density of a subset of the integer grid avoiding the relevant $k$-in-a-row configurations, and let $3\mathbb{N}$ denote the positive multiples of $3$. **Strict grid-density conjecture.** For every $k\in 3\mathbb{N}$,

$$
D(k,\mathbb{Z}^2)<1-\frac{2}{k}.
$$

The source establishes the corresponding upper bound $D(k,\mathbb{Z}^2)\leq 1-2/k$ and reports strictness for $k=3$ and computational evidence for $k=6$; the conjecture remains open in general.
title: The strict density bound for monochromatic k-in-a-row on the integer grid
source_name: Kuo-Han Ku, “Monochromatic k in a row”, arXiv:2606.12880 (2026).
reason: Ku Conjecture5.1 overlaps held Ku family in bound ledger; its equivalent Conjecture5.3 has prior Johnson1981 exclusion. Selected source passage confirms scope. No repeat sweep or new family proposal.

statement:
Let $D(k,\mathbb{Z}^2)$ and $D(k, (\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z})^2)$ denote the corresponding maximum avoiding densities on the integer grid and the discrete torus, respectively. **Torus-density conjecture.** For every $k\in 3\mathbb{N}$,

$$
D(k,(\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z})^2)<D(k,\mathbb{Z}^2).
$$

The source records the general inequality in the opposite direction, gives strictness at $k=3$, and reports computational evidence at $k=6$; the proposed strict inequality remains open.
title: The strict torus-to-grid density inequality for monochromatic k-in-a-row
source_name: Kuo-Han Ku, “Monochromatic k in a row”, arXiv:2606.12880 (2026).
reason: Ku Conjecture5.2 is same held torus family; narrow k6 Conjecture5.4 route already held and generic lower bounds excluded. Preserve prior objections; no reopening or alternate-witness credit.

statement:
Let $[k]^d$ be the $d$-dimensional grid, with $k\in\mathbb{N}_{\geq 2}$ and $d\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $D(k,[k]^d)$ denote the maximum density of a configuration avoiding the relevant $k$-in-a-row patterns. **Hypercube density conjecture.** For every $k\in\mathbb{N}_{\geq 2}$ and $d\in\mathbb{N}$,

$$
D(k,[k]^d)=1-\frac{2}{k}.
$$

The source motivates this by a construction attaining the value when $k/2$ is a natural number coprime with $d!$; the assertion for all $k$ and $d$ remains open.
title: The hypercube maximum-density conjecture for monochromatic k-in-a-row
source_name: Kuo-Han Ku, “Monochromatic k in a row”, arXiv:2606.12880 (2026).
reason: Universal all k,d equality needs source's precise configuration definition and known even/coprime construction restrictions. Primary Conjecture5.6 matches these quantifiers and source proves d=2; no all-d mechanism found.

statement:
Let $\widetilde M^d$ be a symmetric space with curvature $-1\leq K\leq 0$ and real rank $r$. Let $G$ act on $\widetilde M$, and suppose there is a minimum displacement greater than $f(n)$, meaning

$$
d(gx,x)>f(n)
$$

for every $x\in\widetilde M$ and every $1\neq g\in G$.

**Group-ring resolution conjecture.** There is a function $f(n)$ such that every $n$-generated ideal in $\mathbb K[G]$ has a free resolution of length $r-1$.

Such a resolution property would imply, via the methods of the paper, $k$-cellular waist inequalities for maps from uniform locally symmetric spaces of real rank $r$ whenever $0<k<d-m-(r-1)$. The conjecture extends the hyperbolic-space case, where the corresponding group-ring ideals are free.
title: The group-ring resolution conjecture for symmetric spaces
source_name: Grigori Avramidi and Thomas Delzant, “Cellular waists of hyperbolic spaces”, arXiv:2606.13585 (2026).
reason: Uniform displacement function for every n-generated ideal and arbitrary symmetric rank requires group-ring homological control. Rank1 freeness does not produce length r-1 resolutions for higher rank.

statement:
Let $X = \operatorname{\mathbf{Flag}}(p_1|q_1, \dots, p_t|q_t;\;V)$ be a flag supervariety of type $\tau$, and let $Y$ be the variety associated to $X$ by the construction in the paper. A **compositionality conjecture for partial flag supervarieties.** The variety $Y$ is compositional, with defining parameters $\Delta_\bullet$ of the form

$$
\Delta_h = \sum c^h_i p_i + d^h_i q_i,
$$

where $c^h_i,d^h_i \in \mathbf{Z}$ depend only on $\tau$ and are independent of the $p_i$ and $q_i$. This is motivated by calculations in the $2$-step case and by the extension result; the conjecture asserts that the rank conditions arising from arbitrary compositions completely determine the relevant compositional variety for all partial flag supervarieties.
title: Compositionality conjecture for partial flag supervarieties
source_name: Abhik Pal, “Cohomology of Flag Superschemes and Syzygies of Compositional Varieties”, arXiv:2606.14953 (2026).
reason: Compositionality and associated Y need source rank-condition definitions for arbitrary flag type; two-step calculations do not control all compositions. No small exact algebraic certificate available from literal record.

statement:
Let $k\geq 3$ be an integer. A $k$-uniform hypergraph is **linear** if it contains no $2$-cycle, and let $\alpha({\mathcal H})$ denote its independence number. **Shattering-threshold conjecture.** For every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists $\Delta_0\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, for every $\Delta\geq\Delta_0$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}$, every $n$-vertex $k$-uniform linear hypergraph ${\mathcal H}$ of maximum degree $\Delta$ satisfies

$$
\alpha({\mathcal H})\geq (1-\varepsilon)n\left(\frac{1}{k-1}\frac{\log\Delta}{\Delta}\right)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}.
$$

This is presented as a stronger form of the linear-hypergraph conjecture above. Existing approaches rely on random sampling to reduce to the high-girth setting, and the source says that resolving it requires substantially new ideas.
title: Shattering-threshold conjecture for independent sets in linear hypergraphs
source_name: Abhishek Dhawan, Abhishek Methuku and Minh-Quan Vo, “The independence number of uncrowded hypergraphs: bounds matching the shattering threshold”, arXiv:2606.18048 (2026).
reason: Asymptotically sharp independence bound for all linear k-uniform hypergraphs and all sufficiently large Delta needs an optimal constant. High-girth sampling loses the desired constant; no repair found.

statement:
Let $X$ be a finite simplicial complex, let $csigma_{\max}(\partial_k)$ denote the largest singular value of its $k$-th boundary operator, and let $L_k^{\mathrm{up}}$ denote the $k$-dimensional upper Laplacian. **Monotonicity conjecture.** For every finite simplicial complex and every $k\geq 1$, one has

$$
\sigma_{\max}(\partial_{k+1})\leq\sigma_{\max}(\partial_k);
$$

equivalently, $\lambda_{\max}(L_k^{\mathrm{up}})$ is non-increasing in $k$. The conjecture proposes a uniform higher-dimensional extension of the comparison studied for graphs; its status is not determined by the supplied text.
title: Monotonicity conjecture for the largest upper-Laplacian eigenvalue
source_name: Suil O, “An upper bound on the largest eigenvalue of the Helmholtzian of a graph”, arXiv:2606.19742 (2026).
reason: Primary Conjecture5.2 matches every finite complex and k>=1. Theorem4.2 body gives only mu+(n-mu)/(k+2); missing-face overcounting loses the required factor. No small counterexample or sharp inequality found, so no spectral formal chain investment.

statement:
Let $G=(K,S)$ be a split graph, where $K$ is a clique and $S$ is an independent set. A **star $k$-coloring** is a star coloring using at most $k$ colors.

**Linear-time certifying algorithm conjecture.** For every fixed positive integer $k$, there is a certifying algorithm that runs in time

$$
O(|V|+|E|)
$$

to determine whether an input split graph $G$ admits a star $k$-coloring.

The conjecture is motivated by explicit certifying algorithms for the cases treated earlier in the paper and by the apparent extendability of their structural proofs to every fixed $k$. The supplied text does not provide a proof for arbitrary $k$.
title: Linear-time certifying algorithm conjecture for star coloring of split graphs
source_name: Germán Benítez-Bobadilla, Fernando Esteban Contreras-Mendoza, César Hernández-Cruz, Cláudia Linhares Sales and Ana Trujillo-Negrete, “Star Coloring on Some Subclasses of Chordal Graphs”, arXiv:2606.25168 (2026).
reason: Primary Props3.1–3.2 give clique threshold and extension after deleting dominated independent vertices. For fixed k retain maximal neighborhood types, at most binom(k,floor(k/2)), brute-force the constant kernel, extend a coloring or return the uncolorable kernel as certificate. Linear preprocessing via at most 2^k masks gives full scope, but is a short direct adaptation of source lemmas; no discovery proposal.

statement:
Let $N_{\alpha}(d)$ denote the maximum number of equiangular lines in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with common angle $\arccos(\alpha)$.

**Balla's conjecture for $1/\alpha$ is odd.** For every integer $k\geq 1$ and every $d\geq 1$,

$$
N_{\frac{1}{2k+1}}(d)\leq \max\left\{\binom{4k^2+4k}{2},\left\lfloor\frac{(k+1)(d-1)}{k}\right\rfloor\right\}.
$$

The paper presents this as the natural remaining question after proving Balla's general conjecture in two cases and disproving it for infinitely many values of $\alpha$. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
title: Balla's conjecture for reciprocal odd integers
source_name: Chuanyuan Ge and Shiping Liu, “New bounds for equiangular lines and Balla's conjecture”, arXiv:2606.29392 (2026).
reason: All reciprocal odd angles and every dimension require an exact equiangular-line bound. Known non-odd reciprocal counterexamples do not touch this restricted domain; no suitable Gram/Seidel witness found.

statement: Let $G$ be a graph, and let $\Delta(G)$ denote its maximum degree. A **clique of size $\Delta(G)$** is a complete subgraph on $\Delta(G)$ vertices. **Cranston–Rabern's list-coloring conjecture.** Every graph $G$ with $\Delta(G)\geq 9$ and no clique of size $\Delta(G)$ is $(\Delta(G)-1)$-choosable. The supplied text says the conjecture is known for claw-free graphs and remains open when $9\leq\Delta(G)\leq 68$ under the same condition.
title: Cranston–Rabern list Borodin–Kostochka conjecture
source_name: Nandana K Vasudevan, K Somasundaram and N Narayanan, “List-Coloring and Chromatic-Choosability – A Dynamic Survey”, arXiv:2606.31702 (2026).
reason: Every graph with Delta>=9 and forbidden Delta-clique must be (Delta-1)-choosable for arbitrary lists. Claw-free and large-Delta cases do not cover all graphs in the remaining degree band.

statement:
Let $[t]^n$ be the set of words of length $n$ over an alphabet of size $t$, let $r$ be the number of colors, and let $\mathrm{HJ}^{[k]}(t,r)$ denote the least dimension forcing a monochromatic line in the $k$-th bracket class, with value $\infty$ if no such dimension exists. Let $\mathrm{HJ}(t,r)$ be the Hales–Jewett number, and let $\kappa_{\mathrm{all}}(t,r)$ be the largest bracket level whose line-free colorings exist in every dimension. **Collapse conjecture.**

$$
\mathrm{HJ}^{[\mathrm{HJ}(t,r)-1]}(t,r)=\infty
$$

for all $t,r\ge2$; equivalently, $\kappa_{\mathrm{all}}(t,r)=\mathrm{HJ}(t,r)-1$. This is known wherever the relevant Hales–Jewett numbers are known, but remains open in general.
title: Collapse conjecture for the Hales–Jewett bracket hierarchy
source_name: Younes Mouhib, “One-Weight Colorings, the Symmetric Class, and Lower Bounds for Hales–Jewett Numbers”, arXiv:2607.02226 (2026).
reason: Requires line-free colorings in every dimension at bracket level HJ(t,r)-1 for every t,r>=2. Known HJ numbers or finite colorings do not yield a uniform hierarchy-collapse construction.

statement:
Let $f_2(k)$ be the smallest positive integer $n$ such that every 2-coloring of $\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$ has a monochromatic solution, with the variables not necessarily distinct, to

$$
\frac{1}{x_1}+\frac{1}{x_2}+\cdots+\frac{1}{x_k}=\frac{1}{x_{k+1}}.
$$

Call $k$ an odd prime power if $k=p^m$ for some odd prime number $p$ and positive integer $m$. **Equality conjecture.** If $k\geq4$ is not an odd prime power, then

$$
f_2(k)=3k^2.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by computational results showing that $f_2(k)=3k^2$ exactly when $k$ is an odd prime power for $k\in\{3,4,\ldots,25\}$, together with the proved result that $f_2(k)=3k^2$ when $k=3\cdot2^m$ for a positive integer $m$ and that $f_2(k)\geq3k^2+1$ for odd prime powers.
title: The characterization of equality in the two-color reciprocal Rado number
source_name: Collier Gaiser and Mojtaba Ramezanpour, “A sharp lower bound for some reciprocal Rado numbers”, arXiv:2607.04373 (2026).
reason: Record's computational explanation says equality exactly at odd prime powers while its last clause says strict inequality there; source comparison needed. Quantified non-prime-power claim is not refuted by this prose inconsistency. No reciprocal-Rado coloring certificate constructed.

statement:
Let $d\geq 3$, and let $p:[n]\to\mathbb{R}^d$ satisfy

$$
\|p(i)\|=1
$$

for all $i\in[n]$ and

$$
\sum_{i=1}^n p(i)=0.
$$

Assume that the image of $p$ has size at least $3$. **Lew–Noy–Plaza–Eberhardt's conjecture.** The second largest eigenvalue of $L(K_n,p)$ is

$$
\frac{n}{2},
$$

and its multiplicity is exactly $n-1$. This conjecture asks whether the lower bound from the preceding result is sharp and whether $n/2$ has an extremal spectral interpretation for stiffness matrices of complete frameworks under the stated spherical normalization; its resolution is not indicated here.
title: Lew–Noy–Plaza–Eberhardt conjecture on the second largest eigenvalue of normalized complete frameworks
source_name: Tingting Wang and Lu Lu, “The Second Largest Eigenvalue of Stiffness Matrices of Normalized Complete Frameworks”, arXiv:2607.05472 (2026).
reason: Need exact stiffness-matrix normalization, collisions and second-largest eigenvalue counting convention. Coplanar images and repeated points may alter multiplicity but cannot be used before the source definitions; no eigenvalue claim made.

statement: For a digraph $D$, its minimum out-degree is the minimum number of outgoing edges over all vertices of $D$. **Lichiardopol's conjecture.** For every $k\geq1$, there exists an integer $g(k)$ such that every digraph of minimum out-degree at least $g(k)$ contains $k$ vertex-disjoint directed cycles of distinct lengths. The source states that this directed analogue is famously open and is not known for any minimum out-degree condition depending only on $k$.
title: Lichiardopol's minimum out-degree conjecture for directed cycles of distinct lengths
source_name: J. Pascal Gollin, Maximilian Gorsky, Meike Hatzel, Kevin Hendrey, Tony Huynh, Caleb McFarland, Marek Sokołowski, Sebastian Wiederrecht and Paul Wollan, “An Erdős-Pósa theorem for cycles and faces of distinct lengths”, arXiv:2607.06869 (2026).
reason: For every k needs some minimum-outdegree threshold forcing disjoint directed cycles with all distinct lengths. k1 or ordinary cycle packing cannot bridge simultaneous length distinctions.

statement:
For $d\in\mathbb{N}$, let $G(d)$ be the infimum of $\bar{t}(G)/|E(G)|$ over all finite unit-distance digraphs $G$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with $|E(G)|>0$, where $\bar{t}(G)$ is the maximum number of edges in a subgraph without any directed cyclic triangles. A digraph is **unit-distance** if every edge $xy$ satisfies $\lVert x-y\rVert_2=1$.

**Exponential convergence conjecture.** There exist absolute constants $c>0$ and $d_0\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, for all $d\geqslant d_0$,

$$
G(d)\leqslant \frac{1}{2}+\exp(-cd).
$$

This conjecture would give an exponentially sharp upper bound for the extremal density of $\Delta$-free subsets of high-dimensional spheres, complementing the paper's polynomial upper bound and its connection between such sets and triangle-free unit-distance digraphs.
title: The exponential convergence conjecture for triangle-free unit-distance digraphs
source_name: Anubhab Ghosal and Dmitry Tsarev, “On the largest size of sum-free sets in symmetric regions”, arXiv:2607.07991 (2026).
reason: Record's solved label is not proof evidence. All sufficiently large dimensions require a unit-distance digraph construction with exponential convergence, not merely arbitrary dense digraphs; primary body unread.

statement:
Let $H$ be a planar graph and let $k$ be a positive integer. A graph is **$kH$-free** if it contains no $k$ pairwise non-adjacent independent $H$-minor models. MIS denotes the Maximum Independent Set problem.

**Independent-planar-minor MIS conjecture.** For every planar $H$ and every $k$, MIS is polynomial-time solvable on the class of $kH$-free graphs.

The paper proves an $n^{O(\log n)}$-time algorithm for this problem, so the conjecture asks whether the quasi-polynomial bound can always be improved to polynomial time. It remains open in the $2K_3$-free case.
title: Polynomial-time MIS conjecture for graphs forbidding independent planar minors
source_name: Maria Chudnovsky, Amadeus Reinald and Stéphan Thomassé, “Forbidding anticomplete planar minors: Induced Erdős–Pósa property and Maximum Independent Set in QP”, arXiv:2607.09646 (2026).
reason: For each fixed planar H and k need polynomial-time MIS on graphs forbidding anticomplete minor models. Quasi-polynomial recursion and easy H cases do not establish a polynomial exponent uniformly over input size.

statement:
Let $T=(t_n)_{n\ge0}$ be the steering word considered in the paper, and let $p_T(k)$ denote the number of distinct factors of length $k$ occurring in $T$. **Exact complexity conjecture.**

$$
p_T(k)=3^{\,k+1}-2^{\,k+1}\quad\text{for every }k\ge1.
$$

The formula agrees with the measured complexity profile for small $k$ and predicts the exact number of factors at every length. The paper presents it as conjectural; in particular, the available computation is finite and does not establish the assertion for all $k$.
title: The exact factor-complexity formula for the $(3/2)^n$ steering word
source_name: Ralf Stephan, “Superlinear complexity of the (3/2)^n steering word”, arXiv:2607.11648 (2026).
reason: Primary v1 Definition1.2 recovered exact half-up rounded steering letters; bound text search did not locate the stated exact exponential formula in this fetched body. Exact 2000-term counts match k<=3 but miss one k4 factor; finite absence is no refutation. All-length factor realization remains unsupported; source/version qualification HOLD.

statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, and let the **$k$th power** of a Hamilton cycle be the graph obtained by joining every pair of vertices whose distance along the cycle is at most $k$. Let $\delta(G)$ denote the minimum degree of $G$.

**Seymour's conjecture.** For positive integers $n$ and $k$ with $n\geq k+1$ and $k\geq2$, if

$$
\delta(G)\geq\frac{k}{k+1}n,
$$

then $G$ contains the $k$th power of a Hamilton cycle.

This generalizes Pósa's conjecture and Dirac's theorem by prescribing a minimum-degree threshold for every power of a Hamilton cycle. The supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.
title: Seymour's conjecture on powers of Hamilton cycles
source_name: Zhilan Wang, Shuo Wei and Jin Yan, “The exact total degree threshold for the square of a Hamilton cycle in digraphs”, arXiv:2607.13831 (2026).
reason: Every n>=k+1 with exact degree threshold is stronger than sufficiently-large-n Hamilton-power theorems. Small exceptions or cycle-convention corrections would not count; no general constructive route found.

statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, let $i(G)$ be the size of a smallest maximal independent set, and let $\tau(G)$ be the transversal number of the family of maximal independent sets. Define

$$
\beta(G)=\frac{\tau(G)i(G)}{n}.
$$

**Beta conjecture.** For all graphs $G$ on $n$ vertices,

$$
\beta(G)=o(n).
$$

This is presented as a reformulation of the Bollobás–Erdős–Tuza conjecture for $c$-hollow graphs. The paper notes that it holds trivially when $i(G)=o(n)$, while the general assertion remains open.
title: The beta conjecture for maximal independent sets
source_name: Joshua Cooper and Isaiah Hollars, “Hitting all maximal independent sets in c-hollow graphs”, arXiv:2607.15486 (2026).
reason: Uniform sublinear beta means supremum over graph sequences; i=o(n) trivial case does not address i linear in n. Metadata refuted label supplies no counterexample. Need source body and an explicit family with both hitting and independent-domination parameters large.

statement:
Let $T_0,T_1,T_2,\dots$ denote the threshold sequence used to define the middle regimes, and let $W^*(n,m)$ be the minimum internal wall measure for tilings of an $n\times n$ square by $m$ rectangles with pairwise distinct dimensions. The middle regime for $m$ is

$$
T_{m-2}\le n<T_{m-1}.
$$

**Middle-regime doubling conjecture.** For every $m\ge4$ and every $n$ in this middle regime,

$$
W^*(n,m)=n+2(m-2).
$$

The formula is established in the source for $m\in\{4,5\}$ by case analysis and for $m=6$ by exhaustive certification; the conjecture remains open for general $m\ge7$.
title: The middle-regime doubling conjecture for distinct rectangle tilings
source_name: Diego Lago Gómez, “The minimum surface area of k unequal boxes tiling a cube: sharp thresholds, a fault-free law, and a reduction to two dimensions”, arXiv:2607.15894 (2026).
reason: Threshold T_j and distinct-dimensions conventions are source-defined. m4,5,6 already known; full m>=7 wall-minimizing tilings need matching construction and lower bound across every middle regime.

statement:
Let $P^+(n)$ denote the largest prime factor of $n$. For $a,b\in[0,1]$, define

$$
B(x;a,b):=\#\{n\leq x:P^+(n)\leq x^a,\ P^+(n+1)\leq x^b\}.
$$

Let $\rho(t)$ denote the Dickman–de Bruijn function. **Erdős–Pomerance conjecture.** For every $a,b\in[0,1]$,

$$
\lim_{x\rightarrow\infty}x^{-1}B(x;a,b)=\rho\left(\frac{1}{a}\right)\rho\left(\frac{1}{b}\right).
$$

This formalizes the conjectured independence of the largest prime factors of consecutive integers and implies the Erdős–Turán conjecture. Its resolution status is not specified in the supplied text, and it remains open here.
title: Erdős–Pomerance conjecture on independent largest prime factors
source_name: Zhiyuan Yang, “An improvement on the largest prime factors of consecutive integers”, arXiv:2607.16032 (2026).
reason: Joint Dickman distribution for consecutive integers at all a,b is substantive independence, not marginal smooth-number asymptotics. a=0 convention is a wording issue only; no all-parameter analytic route.

statement:
Fix an arbitrary integer $k\geq 2$, and let $a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_k$ be any permutation of $0,1,\ldots,k-1$. Let $P^+(m)$ denote the largest prime factor of $m$. **De Koninck–Doyon conjecture.** As $x$ tends to infinity,

$$
\#\{n\leq x:P^+(n+a_1)<P^+(n+a_2)<\cdots<P^+(n+a_k)\}\sim\frac{1}{k!}x.
$$

This generalizes the Erdős–Turán ordering conjecture from two consecutive integers to every ordering of $k$ consecutive integers. The supplied text does not report a resolution, so the conjecture remains open here.
title: De Koninck–Doyon conjecture on orderings of largest prime factors
source_name: Zhiyuan Yang, “An improvement on the largest prime factors of consecutive integers”, arXiv:2607.16032 (2026).
reason: Every fixed k and every ordering need density 1/k! among consecutive largest prime factors. Symmetry heuristics and k2 estimates do not imply full joint independence; no tractable full-scope mechanism.

statement:
Let $A_n(D)$ be the maximum cardinality of a subset $\mathcal F\subseteq\mathbb Z^n$ whose diameter in the anticode metric $d_{\mathrm a}$ is at most $D$. Let $S_{n,D}$ be the simplex-shaped anticode, and write $P_D=\lfloor D/2\rfloor$ and $Q_D=\lceil D/2\rceil$. **Optimal anticode conjecture.** For all integers $n,D\ge0$, 

$$
A_n(D)=M_n(D)\coloneq |S_{n,D}| =\sum_{j=0}^n\binom nj\binom{P_D}{j} \binom{Q_D+n-j}{n-j}.
$$

The theorem established in dimension three proves this equality when $n=3$, while the conjecture asks for the corresponding optimality of the simplex construction in every dimension.
title: The optimal simplex anticode conjecture in $A_n$
source_name: Mladen Kovačević, “An Isodiametric Theorem and Lattice Diameter-Perfect Codes in A_3”, arXiv:2607.21037 (2026).
reason: Primary Conjecture7.1 exact all n,D recovered; Proposition7.2 and Lemma7.3 reduce to fixed-ground-set high-intersection multisets. 3003 exact unbalanced-simplex comparisons found no improvement, but do not examine arbitrary anticodes. Dimension3 slab/K4 proof does not extend automatically; general structural bound missing.
